chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Muthanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Karib al-Sayrafi, who said:

We were a group who bought a bird, so we clipped its wings and entered Mecca with it. The people of Mecca faulted that upon us. So Karib sent to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him, so he said: 'Entrust it to a Muslim man from the people of Mecca, or a Muslim woman. So when its wings grow straight (are restored), free its way.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for bringing a clipped bird into Mecca during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of the prohibition against keeping game within the Haram boundaries, offering a pragmatic solution of temporary custodianship to avoid expiation. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the sacred precincts while accommodating the realities of pilgrimage, reflecting the Imams' nuanced approach to fiqh. The ruling underscores the principle that the restriction applies to the state of possession within the boundary rather than the mere presence of the animal.
